messages.subject: Stan 2.6.0 bug?
parts:
- I took a model https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/blob/master/bugs_examples/vol1/stacks/stacks_a_normal.stan
- I added test data there to get the attached model (the attached model is with the minimal changes from the original model which reproduces the problem, without including other changes I have made)
- The model code compiles with both 2.5.0 and 2.6.0.
- I've attached R dump data file produced by MatlbStan.
- MatlabStan uses following command for sampling (using the R dump file for data)
stacks_a_normal_orig_zt sample num_samples=1000 num_warmup=1000 save_warmup=0 thin=1 adapt engaged=1 gamma=0.05 delta=0.8 kappa=0.75 t0=10 init_buffer=75 term_buffer=50 window=25 algorithm=hmc engine=nuts max_depth=10 metric=diag_e stepsize=1 stepsize_jitter=0 id=1 data file=temp.data.R init=2 random seed=209475 output file=stacks-1 diagnostic_file= refresh=100

- The sampling runs fine with 2.5.0, but fails with 2.6.0 giving the following error
> stackscv-1: Exception: []: accessing element out of range. index 2 out of range; expecting index to
> be between 1 and 1; index position = 2zt


Can someone else reproduce this error?

Aki

> It is also strange that CmdStan and RStan have different requirements for the dump file.

Sorry about that.

In R, the "dump" file is just R source code, so it can
have arbitrar bits of R in it. I just pulled out the
relevant formatting, not even realizing that R doesn't
even print its dump formats uniformly (it has little
tricks inside that presumably try to shorten the output).

So we have a Stan-specific dump method in R.

We're going to be moving to either protocolo buffers
or JSON or both in the future.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Stan 2.6.0 bug?
parts:
It's a problem in R the way Aki had it and the fix is the
one Jonah suggested.

The root cause is that R conflates a length-1 array and a scalar.
So even if I do this:

a <- c(1)

R treats this as synonymous with

a <- 1

Stan is pickier with its types, requiring an array. The dump
file you provide is fine with CmdStan, but when you call in R directly,
you need to force it to treat a as an array of size 1 rather than
a scalar, as Jonah demonstrated:

Yt <- array(42, dim=1)

- Bob

but not with
p <- 3
N <- 2

Y <- c(1, 2)

Aki

1) Yt <- array(42, dim=1) did not work with CmdStan (2.6)
2) Yt <- structure(c(42), .Dim = c(1)) did work with CmdStan (2.6)
3) the error I reported should not depend on definition of Yt, because the line producing the error does not have anything to do with Yt!
    the error messages refers to zt, which is not data and doesn't come from the dump file

Aki

On Thursday, March 5, 2015 at 12:10:13 AM UTC+2, Bob Carpenter wrote:
It's a problem in R the way Aki had it and the fix is the
one Jonah suggested.

The root cause is that R conflates a length-1 array and a scalar.
So even if I do this:

  a <- c(1)

R treats this as synonymous with

  a <- 1

Stan is pickier with its types, requiring an array.  The dump
file you provide is fine with CmdStan, but when you call in R directly,
you need to force it to treat a as an array of size 1 rather than
a scalar, as Jonah demonstrated:

  Yt <- array(42, dim=1)

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan 2.6.0 bug?
parts:
Thanks for being persistent Aki!

That's definitely a bug. I reproduced on the latest dev versions
of CmdStan and Stan with a minimal example I pasted into a
new issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1342

It's definitely not an I/O issue as both programs were able
to read the data and print it out just fine. The error
is in the transformed data assignment of the variable z.

Now I have no clue at all as to why the size of the matrices
matters. That's the only difference in the two programs (other
than that the matrix isn't square in the second example.

I assigned it to Daniel because my guess is it has something
to do with the refactoring of error handling types that was
going to treat indexing errors differently. But I can also
try to figure out what's going on if Daniel doesn't have time.

I think we should fix this one before the next release, so I
labeled it as such.

- Bob
